chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Al-Hasan ibn Atiyya, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man from among our non-companions gifted me Bukhtuj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he is from those who consider the intoxicant permissible, do not drink it; and if he is from those who do not consider its drinking permissible, accept it,' or he said: 'Drink it.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions, referring to the Shia followers.
key_terms.الْبُخْتُجَ: Bukhtuj, a concentrated grape juice or syrup, often used as a precursor to wine but not necessarily intoxicating in its pure form.
key_terms.الْمُسْكِرَ: The intoxicant (or that which causes intoxication).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on drinking a gift of grape juice from a non-Shia person who may or may not consider intoxicants permissible?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia principle of *Istishab al-Hal* (presumption of continuity of the original state), where the gift is presumed pure unless proven otherwise, but the recipient's consumption is linked to the giver's theological stance (*Ahliyyah*) on intoxicants. It highlights the nuance between the physical purity of the substance and the spiritual or legal validity of accepting it based on the giver's adherence to Islamic law, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding gifts from non-Shias.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Hassan Bin Atiyya, from Umar Bin Yazeed who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The man, from other that our companions, gifted to me Al-Bukhtuj (boiled grape juice)’. So heasws said: ‘If he was from the one who permits the intoxicants, so do not drink it, and if he was from the ones who does not permit drinking it, so accept it’, or said: ‘Drink it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Hassan ibn ‘Atiyyah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who recommends the use of boiled juice (grape juice) and he is not one of our people. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is one who considers intoxicating substances lawful, then do not use it but if he considers it unlawful then you can use it for drink,’ or that he (the Imam) said, ‘You can drink it.’”
